title: Parvati in the snows
hookLine: the daughter of the mountain wins Shiva with years of tapas, not tricks; why women fast on Teej
last: THE EGO LIFTS; THE DEVOTEE BOWS.

cards: Himalaya, the mountain king, has a daughter, and her name tells you whose she is: Parvati, daughter of the mountain. She has set her heart on Shiva, who sits on Kailash smeared in ash, eyes closed, wanting nothing.

The gods already tried to wake him with Kama, the god of love, and it went badly: one look from Shiva's third eye, and Kama was ash. So Parvati stops trying to be noticed. She does something much harder.

teach.h: TAPAS: THE HEAT OF A PRACTICE KEPT UP.
teach.b: She climbs into the high snows and begins tapas: the heat of a practice kept up, day after day. In the poet Kalidasa's telling, she stands in icy water on winter nights and sits between fires under the summer sun.
She eats less and less, until she lives on fallen leaves, and then gives up even those.
That's why one of her names is Aparna: the one without even a leaf. Years pass. Then a young ascetic with matted hair walks into her clearing.
Why waste yourself on Shiva? he asks. He lives in cremation grounds. He wears snakes.
Parvati's eyes flash. You don't know him, she says. My heart is set, and I won't hear another word.
She turns to go. And the stranger stops her: he is Shiva himself, in disguise.

teach.h: I'M YOURS, WON BY YOUR TAPAS.
teach.b: From today, he says, I'm yours, won by your tapas. Hindus still keep this story, with a fast.

teach.h: HARTALIKA TEEJ: THE FAST THAT REMEMBERS.
teach.b: On Hartalika Teej, many women, especially in north India, Maharashtra and Nepal, fast all day, some without even water, in memory of Parvati's tapas, and worship Shiva and Parvati together.
The teaching is tapas: steady effort, offered to God, is a heat that burns something away. Parvati didn't win Shiva by being noticed. She won him by keeping going.
Now look back at your year. Three hundred thirty-one days, a few minutes each, mostly unseen.
That's a small tapas. And from here you can see the next range: tomorrow, year two opens an Upanishad that begins with one sound, om.

how: On Hartalika Teej many Hindu women fast, some without water, and worship Shiva and Parvati in memory of her tapas; others keep vrats, vowed fasts, such as Monday fasts for Shiva.

o: the world's highest single mountain peak
a sacred river flowing down from the snows
the abode of snow: the great range still ahead

p: the heat of a practice kept up

s: Parvati won Shiva by having Kama shoot him with love
that ended in ash. she won him with years of tapas in the snows.
the young ascetic who mocked Shiva was Shiva in disguise
he was testing her. when she defended him and turned to go, he showed himself.
on Hartalika Teej many women fast, some without water, remembering Parvati
and they worship Shiva and Parvati together.

games.q: you're Parvati, years into your tapas. a stranger says Shiva isn't worth it. what do you do?
o: agree and go home: he has a point.
defend Shiva and keep your vow.
argue until the stranger gives up.
games.why: she defends Shiva, refuses to hear more, and turns to go. the stranger is Shiva, won by her tapas.

practice: Last sit of year one. Sit tall, the way Parvati sat in the snow. Think of one small thing you kept up this year, a minute a day, a lamp, a word, a habit, and feel the warmth it built; tapas means heat.
If you pray, offer it to Shiva and Parvati, or to God by whatever name you use, and ask for steadiness for the next range. If you don't, just thank the you who kept showing up.

wordCard.voice: Himalaya, the abode of snow: Parvati's father, the mountain king, and the snows where she kept her tapas. The next range is behind it, and you climb it the way she did, one day at a time.

orig.note: Sanskrit himālaya: hima, snow, + ālaya, abode: the abode of snow, the great range.

carryVoice: Your line: tapas, love that keeps going. That's day three hundred thirty-one, and year one.

sources.ref: Kalidasa, Kumarasambhava, canto 5 (Parvati's tapas; Aparna; the disguised student; Shiva's reply)
Shiva Purana, Rudra Samhita, Parvati Khanda (Parvati's tapas and Shiva's test)
